sources.title: Detecting and Defending Against Seizure-Inducing GIFs in Social Media, Author PDF
sources.notes: Supervisor directly downloaded and text-extracted the author-hosted PDF. Section 5 Evaluation states that simulated GIFs have known ground truth, while randomized and potentially dangerous GIFs collected in the wild have unknown ground truth. The paper describes binary risk-tool consensus and deliberately does not publish the potentially dangerous dataset. It contains no spatial mask annotation method, temporal-region adjudication rule, annotator agreement procedure, or reusable actual-risk gold labels.

sources.title: A new adaptive temporal filter: application to photosensitive seizure patients
sources.published_or_version: Psychiatry and Clinical Neurosciences 54(6), 2000-12; PMID 11145469; DOI 10.1046/j.1440-1819.2000.00770.x
sources.notes: Issuer surface: NLM PubMed record for the primary study by Nomura et al. Exact locator: Abstract. Eleven photosensitive epilepsy patients were exposed to a four-second 12 Hz red/blue Pocket Monster scene on a 14-inch television at 2 m; all showed generalized PPR on the unfiltered scene and none on the adaptively filtered scene. PubMed supplies bibliographic metadata and abstract access, not a license to redistribute the publisher's full article; only the citation and atomic findings are recorded.

sources.title: Incidence of photosensitive epilepsy in unselected Indian epileptic population
sources.notes: Issuer surface: NLM PubMed record for the primary screening study by Saleem et al. Exact locator: Abstract. The study screened 1,000 unselected epilepsy patients from Northern India using clinical history and an IPS EEG protocol, finding six photosensitive patients; only three reported visually provoked seizures and the observed IPS response range was 6 to 60 cycles/s. PubMed does not grant redistribution rights for the publisher's full article.

sources.title: Wind turbines, flicker, and photosensitive epilepsy: characterizing the flashing that may precipitate seizures and optimizing guidelines to prevent them
sources.notes: Issuer surface: NLM PubMed record for the primary risk-modeling study by Harding, Harding and Wilkins. Exact locator: Abstract. The study applies contrast, frequency, mark-space ratio, retinal area and visual-cortex involvement to wind-turbine shadow flicker and argues that frequency should be limited to three flashes/s. This is an environment-specific model, not a clinical validation of FlashPatch or a universal safe-harbor. PubMed does not grant redistribution rights for the publisher's full article.

Exact locators: Abstract; 3.4 More Complex Tests; 4.4 Going Beyond Simple Alternating Frames; 4.5 Including Confounding Characteristics; 5 Open-Source Tool Development; 6 Conclusion. The manuscript says prior synthetic tests have low case coverage and specifies uneven timing, alternating-transition polarity, same-pixel overlap, asynchronous confounds, multi-frame transition duration and synchronization as validation cases. PMC access does not by itself grant redistribution of the publisher version; atomic findings and citation are recorded.
